intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

selected_hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Walking Tour
experiences.description: Start your Istanbul journey with a guided walking tour of the iconic Hagia Sophia and the nearby Blue Mosque. Both landmarks are within walking distance of each other in Sultanahmet, making this ideal even after a late arrival on Day 1 — a leisurely evening stroll around the illuminated exteriors sets the tone without requiring a full day. Dive deep into Byzantine and Ottoman history with a local guide who brings the layers of civilization to life.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Market Exploration
experiences.description: Wander through the world's oldest and largest covered markets. The Grand Bazaar offers over 4,000 shops selling ceramics, textiles, and jewelry, while the nearby Egyptian Spice Bazaar is a feast for the senses with exotic spices, Turkish delight, and dried fruits. Engage with local vendors, practice bargaining, and sample complimentary teas. Both markets are centrally located in Eminönü, close to Sultanahmet hotels, making it easy to pop in and out across multiple days.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class in Beyoğlu
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in the vibrant Beyoğlu neighborhood. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as meze platters, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), lentil soup, and baklava. Classes typically include a market visit to source fresh ingredients, giving you an authentic taste of Istanbul's culinary culture. Beyoğlu is well-connected and centrally located, reducing transit time from most recommended hotel hubs.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the opulent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view sacred relics, and take a guided tour of the Harem — the private royal quarters. The palace sits directly in Sultanahmet, making it easily accessible from centrally located hotels and perfect for a full morning immersion into Ottoman history without long commutes.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Tasting
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, gliding between Europe and Asia with views of Ottoman palaces, fortresses, and the city skyline. After docking, join a guided street food walk along the Karaköy waterfront sampling simit (sesame bread rings), balık ekmek (fish sandwiches), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and Turkish tea. This experience combines history, scenery, and authentic local flavors in one evening outing, departing from the central Eminönü or Karaköy piers.
experiences.location: Karaköy & Eminönü waterfront, Golden Horn, Istanbul

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus (cheapest option, ~₺100) or Metro M11 to central Istanbul, then transfer to Sultanahmet. Check in to your boutique stay in Sultanahmet.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a gentle orientation walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hagia Sophia from outside — both free to view from the square. Stroll through the Hippodrome of Constantinople and see the ancient Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Wander down to the waterfront along Kennedy Caddesi for a sunset view of the Bosphorus. Return to the neighborhood and explore the lively streets around Divan Yolu for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab a simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street cart near the airport or bus station for under ₺30 — a classic Turkish on-the-go snack.
meals.lunch: Eat at the airport or grab a quick döner kebab wrap from a local fast-food stand near Sultanahmet for around ₺80–120.
meals.dinner: Head to Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi (Historic Sultanahmet Meatball Restaurant) on Divan Yolu — a legendary budget-friendly spot. A plate of köfte with bread and ayran costs around ₺150–200.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Use this time to rest, rehydrate, and get your bearings. Purchase an Istanbulkart (transit card) at the airport or a nearby kiosk — it saves money on all public transport.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (entry is free as it is now an active mosque — dress modestly and bring a headscarf if needed). Arrive early around 9:00 to beat crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and centuries of layered history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to Topkapi Palace — the heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Buy a combined ticket (approx. ₺500–600). Explore the Imperial Gate, the Harem (small extra fee ~₺150), the Treasury with the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and the stunning views of the Bosphorus from the palace terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Gülhane Park adjacent to Topkapi — one of Istanbul's oldest public parks, free entry. Enjoy the greenery and sea views at dusk. Head back toward Sultanahmet for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Have a traditional Turkish breakfast at your boutique hotel if included, or visit a local börek shop (pastry with cheese or spinach) for ₺50–80.
meals.lunch: Eat at a simple lokanta (traditional Turkish cafeteria-style restaurant) near the palace — look for a daily set menu (tabldot) for around ₺120–160 including soup, main, and bread.
meals.dinner: Try Dönerci Şahin Usta near Sultanahmet — generous portions of chicken or lamb döner with rice or bread for ₺100–150. A local favorite with no tourist markup.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays, so visiting today is ideal. Wear comfortable shoes — the palace complex involves a lot of walking on cobblestones. The Harem has timed entry; buy your ticket early.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums — a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Mesopotamian artifacts, and the Museum of the Ancient Orient. Entry is approximately ₺350–400. Located just below Topkapi, it is often overlooked by tourists and rarely crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. Entry is free. Browse the 4,000+ shops selling spices, ceramics, textiles, and jewelry. Practice bargaining but avoid pressure to buy. Focus on the atmosphere and architecture rather than shopping to stay on budget.
day_by_day.evening: Walk downhill from the Grand Bazaar toward the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Browse the aromatic stalls selling teas, spices, Turkish delight, and dried fruits. Watch the sunset over the Golden Horn from the Galata Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Visit a traditional Turkish breakfast café near Sultanahmet — menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers), olives, cheese, and tea for around ₺100–150.
meals.lunch: Grab a balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the famous floating boats moored at Eminönü waterfront — an Istanbul institution at around ₺80–100. Eat with a view of the Bosphorus.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local meyhane (tavern) in the Kumkapı neighborhood (10-minute walk from Sultanahmet) — try meze plates and grilled fish. Budget around ₺200–250 for a satisfying meal with bread and ayran.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays, so Monday is perfect. The Spice Bazaar closes earlier than the Grand Bazaar — aim to arrive by 17:00. Eminönü is a bustling transport hub; keep an eye on your belongings in crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the ancient underground Byzantine water reservoir just steps from your hotel. Entry is approximately ₺350. The atmospheric columns, carp-filled water, and famous Medusa head bases make it unmissable. Arrive at opening (9:00) to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — arguably the most beautiful mosque in Istanbul, designed by architect Sinan in the 16th century. Entry is free. Wander the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including the tombs of Sultan Suleiman and Hürrem Sultan. The hilltop location offers panoramic views over the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Walk down to the Beyazıt neighborhood and explore the lively streets around Istanbul University. Visit the Beyazıt Mosque (free) and the nearby secondhand book market (Sahaflar Çarşısı) if still open.

meals.breakfast: Try a neighborhood fırın (bakery) near your hotel for fresh pogaça (savory pastry), a boiled egg, and çay (tea) for under ₺80.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the student-friendly lokantas near Beyazıt and Istanbul University — a full meal with soup, main course, salad, and bread for ₺100–140.
meals.dinner: Visit Hamdi Restaurant's budget alternative — instead, head to a simple pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) restaurant near Sultanahmet. Cheese or meat pide with ayran costs ₺120–160.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — good thing you visited on Day 2. The Basilica Cistern is a short walk from your hotel, making it a perfect morning start. The Süleymaniye area is slightly uphill — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot (free) and explore the Galata Tower neighborhood (Karaköy). Climb the Galata Tower for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn — entry approximately ₺350. The tower dates to 1348 and is one of the city's most iconic landmarks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up Istiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — the famous pedestrian boulevard in Beyoğlu stretching nearly 1.5 km. Browse bookshops, music stores, and local boutiques. Explore the historic passages (pasaj) branching off the main street such as Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the ornate Avrupa Pasajı. Ride the nostalgic red tram along Istiklal for ₺20.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Taksim Square for a look at the Republic Monument and the lively square atmosphere. Return to Sultanahmet via Metro and tram using your Istanbulkart.

meals.breakfast: Have breakfast at a Karaköy café — the neighborhood is famous for its pastries. Try a classic Karaköy böreği (flaky pastry) with tea for ₺60–90.
meals.lunch: Eat at a meyhane or lokanta off Istiklal Avenue — avoid the main street restaurants which are pricier. Look for a side-street option with a daily menu for ₺130–170.
meals.dinner: Return to Sultanahmet and try lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza with minced meat) at a local spot — two lahmacun with a salad and ayran for around ₺100–130.

day_by_day.notes: The Galata area and Beyoğlu are on the European side's new town — a nice contrast to the historic peninsula. Istiklal Avenue is busiest in the afternoon and evening. The historic red tram runs the full length of Istiklal — a fun and cheap experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Marmaray commuter train or ferry from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side of Istanbul (use Istanbulkart, ~₺20). Explore the charming Üsküdar district — visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque, the Şemsi Pasha Mosque perched right on the waterfront, and the lively local market streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Asian shore toward Kadıköy — about 3 km or take a minibus. Kadıköy is Istanbul's trendiest neighborhood, full of street art, independent cafés, vinyl record shops, and the famous Kadıköy Produce Market (Kadıköy Pazarı). Browse the market stalls and soak up the bohemian local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a ferry back from Kadıköy to Eminönü or Karaköy (approx. ₺20) as the sun sets over the Bosphorus — one of the most beautiful and cheapest experiences in Istanbul. Walk or tram back to Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Grab a traditional breakfast at a Üsküdar tea garden overlooking the Bosphorus — tea, simit, and cheese for ₺60–90.
meals.lunch: Eat at Kadıköy's famous Çiya Sofrası — a legendary lokanta serving regional Anatolian dishes at very reasonable prices. A full meal costs ₺150–200 and the food quality is exceptional.
meals.dinner: Pick up street food in Kadıköy before the ferry — try kokoreç (grilled offal sandwich, a local specialty) or a kumpir (loaded baked potato) for ₺80–120.

day_by_day.notes: Visiting the Asian side gives great perspective on Istanbul's dual-continent identity. Kadıköy is beloved by locals and less touristy than the historic peninsula. The ferry ride at sunset is genuinely magical and costs almost nothing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — a stunning Byzantine church turned mosque featuring some of the finest Byzantine mosaics in the world, dating from the 14th century. Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood, take the tram and a short bus ride (use Istanbulkart). Entry approximately ₺300–350.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls — the 5th-century land walls that protected Constantinople for a thousand years. Stretch nearly 7 km, they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and largely free to explore. Walk a section between Edirnekapı and Yedikule for dramatic views of the crumbling towers and gates.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the center and explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — colorful, historic districts on the Golden Horn shore with Greek Orthodox churches, old synagogues, and charming painted houses. The area is rapidly becoming a hip local destination.

meals.breakfast: Have breakfast at your hotel or grab a warm açma (soft sesame roll) and tea from a neighborhood bakery near Sultanahmet for ₺40–60.
meals.lunch: Eat at a simple lokanta in the Balat neighborhood — a working-class area with very authentic and affordable food. Expect to pay ₺100–140 for a full meal.
meals.dinner: Try a Balat café or return to Sultanahmet for a hearty mercimek çorbası (red lentil soup) with bread and a main dish at a budget restaurant — around ₺130–160.

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church/Kariye Mosque is a bit out of the way but absolutely worth the trip — the mosaics rival those of Ravenna. Friday is the Islamic holy day — the Chora may have prayer times; check ahead. Balat is photogenic and great for a leisurely afternoon wander.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Hamam (Turkish bath) for a budget-friendly traditional hammam experience — look for off-peak morning rates (approx. ₺400–500 for basic bath and scrub). Alternatively, visit the Cemberlitas Hamam near the Grand Bazaar. A hammam is an essential cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beyazıt area more deeply — visit the Beyazıt State Library (free, beautiful historic building), the Column of Constantine (Çemberlitaş, free), and browse the Sahaflar Çarşısı (secondhand book market between the Grand Bazaar and Beyazıt Mosque — free to browse).
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free weekly Whirling Dervishes ceremony at the Hodjapasha Cultural Center or check for free sema performances at local mosques or cultural centers. Alternatively, enjoy a peaceful evening tea at a rooftop café in Sultanahmet with views of the illuminated Blue Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Have a full Turkish breakfast spread at a local Sultanahmet café — olives, tomatoes, cucumber, cheese, eggs, honey, and unlimited tea for ₺120–160.
meals.lunch: Visit the Tarihi Kapalıçarşı Lokantası inside or near the Grand Bazaar — a no-frills workers' cafeteria with excellent value daily specials for ₺100–130.
meals.dinner: Try a manti restaurant near Sultanahmet — manti (Turkish dumplings with yogurt and tomato butter sauce) is a comforting and affordable dish for ₺120–150.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance or arrive early — popular ones fill up on weekends. The hammam experience typically lasts 1.5–2 hours. Check the Hodjapasha Cultural Center website for their free or low-cost dervish ceremony schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus ferry cruise — use your Istanbulkart on the public Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü for a fraction of tourist boat prices. The long Bosphorus route to Anadolu Kavağı and back takes about 6 hours round trip and costs only ₺60–80 each way. Enjoy views of Ottoman palaces, fortresses, and waterside yalı mansions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian side — a charming fishing village at the mouth of the Black Sea. Hike up to the ruined Yoros Castle (small entry fee ~₺50) for spectacular views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Browse the local fish restaurants along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Eminönü (departs Anadolu Kavağı around 15:00 or 17:00 — check schedule). Arrive back at Eminönü at sunset for golden hour views of the historic skyline.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks and simit from a street vendor before boarding the ferry — eat on deck with Bosphorus views. Budget ₺30–50.
meals.lunch: Have fresh grilled fish at one of the simple restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — grilled sea bass or sea bream with salad and bread for ₺200–250. A splurge compared to other days but excellent quality.
meals.dinner: Light dinner back near Sultanahmet — a bowl of soup and a gözleme (stuffed flatbread with cheese and spinach) from a street vendor for ₺80–110.

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's best budget experiences. Check the Şehir Hatları (City Lines) ferry schedule online before the day — the long Bosphorus route runs only a few times daily. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace in Beşiktaş — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, blending European Baroque with Ottoman design. Entry approximately ₺600–700 (includes guided tour of Selamlık and Harem). Take the tram to Kabataş and walk along the waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a bus to the Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, authentic Istanbul district popular with locals. Explore the Beşiktaş fish market, the waterfront promenade, and the area around the Çırağan Palace (now a hotel — free to view from outside). Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) if interested in Ottoman maritime history — entry around ₺100.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or take a bus to Ortaköy — a picturesque waterfront village beneath the Bosphorus Bridge. Browse the Sunday artisan market stalls (may still be partially open Monday evenings), and admire the Ortaköy Mosque dramatically lit against the bridge.

meals.breakfast: Have a simple breakfast at your hotel or a Sultanahmet bakery before heading out — keep it light and quick, around ₺60–80.
meals.lunch: Eat at a lokanta in Beşiktaş near the fish market — fresh and affordable, with fish soup, a main, and bread for ₺130–160.
meals.dinner: Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (giant loaded baked potato stuffed with butter, cheese, and your choice of toppings) — an Istanbul street food institution at ₺100–150. Eat by the waterfront.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — double-check the schedule as it may have changed by 2027. If closed, substitute with a visit to the Istanbul Modern Art Museum in Karaköy (entry ~₺250) and spend more time in Beşiktaş and Ortaköy.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the Topkapi Palace Museum of Islamic Art or revisit any Sultanahmet sites you want to see again at a slower pace. Alternatively, visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) near the Blue Mosque — entry approximately ₺200. It houses remarkable 6th-century Byzantine floor mosaics discovered beneath the historic peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Küçük Ayasofya Mosque (Little Hagia Sophia) — a beautiful 6th-century Byzantine church converted to a mosque, free entry, and far less crowded than the main Hagia Sophia. Walk through the charming neighborhood of Kadırga nearby with its old Ottoman wooden houses and quiet streets.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Arasta Bazaar behind the Blue Mosque — a smaller, less hectic alternative to the Grand Bazaar with quality crafts, ceramics, and carpets. Good for browsing and perhaps a small souvenir purchase. Watch the Blue Mosque light up after dark from the square.

meals.breakfast: Try a menemen breakfast (eggs scrambled with peppers and tomatoes) at a local Sultanahmet café for ₺90–120.
meals.lunch: Visit Karadeniz Pide ve Döner Salonu near Sultanahmet — a simple, beloved spot for Black Sea-style pide and döner at ₺100–140.
meals.dinner: Have dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Sultanahmet with Blue Mosque views — look for set menus or fixed-price options around ₺200–250. A slight splurge but the atmosphere is worth it on a penultimate evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Little Hagia Sophia is a hidden gem that many visitors miss entirely — it gives a sense of the original Byzantine structure without the crowds. The Kadırga neighborhood is authentic and residential — a great contrast to the tourist-heavy areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara. Catch the Şehir Hatları ferry from Kabataş (approx. ₺60–80 each way, use Istanbulkart). Head to Büyükada, the largest island. Rent a bicycle (₺100–150/hour) or take a horse-drawn carriage tour of the Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and hilltop monastery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — hike up to the Aya Yorgi Church and Monastery on the hill for sweeping views of the Sea of Marmara and the Istanbul skyline in the distance. Swim at one of the small beaches if weather permits (May can be warm enough).
day_by_day.evening: Take the late afternoon ferry back to Kabataş and return to Sultanahmet. This is your second-to-last evening — enjoy a leisurely stroll around the illuminated Sultanahmet Square one more time.

meals.breakfast: Have a quick breakfast before the early ferry — simit, cheese, and tea from a Kabataş street vendor for ₺40–60.
meals.lunch: Eat at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — fresh grilled fish, salad, and bread for ₺200–250. Seafood on the islands is a highlight.
meals.dinner: Back in Sultanahmet, have a final casual dinner at a neighborhood kebab house — mixed grill with rice, salad, and bread for ₺150–180.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Şehir Hatları ferry schedule to Büyükada before this day — ferries run regularly but timing matters for maximizing your day. The islands are very popular on weekends; a Wednesday visit means fewer crowds. No motorized vehicles on the islands makes it wonderfully peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit your favorite spot one last time, whether it's the Hagia Sophia, the Bosphorus waterfront, or the Grand Bazaar for any last-minute gifts. Visit a traditional Turkish breakfast café for a proper send-off meal. Pack and check out of your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, spend remaining hours at the Spice Bazaar for last-minute food souvenirs (Turkish tea, spices, lokum/Turkish delight — all affordable and packable). Head to the airport via Havaist bus or Metro M11 — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for travel and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 incredible days of history, culture, and food in one of the world's great cities.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full, leisurely Turkish breakfast spread at a Sultanahmet café as a final Istanbul memory — olives, cheeses, eggs, fresh bread, honey, and unlimited çay for ₺150–180.
meals.lunch: Have a final döner or köfte sandwich near the Spice Bazaar before heading to the airport — ₺80–100.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or onboard — budget accordingly.

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time to get to Istanbul Airport — it is located far from the city center (approximately 45–60 minutes by bus or metro depending on traffic). The Havaist bus from Taksim or the M11 metro from Gayrettepe are the most budget-friendly options. Keep some Turkish Lira for any last transport needs.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Transfer from airport to Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay in Sultanahmet. Allow 45–60 minutes for taxi or Havaist airport bus to Sultanahmet. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory walk around Sultanahmet Square. Admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the Hippodrome of Constantinople with its ancient obelisks. Stroll through the At Meydanı (Hippodrome Park) and soak in the neighborhood atmosphere without overexerting after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the narrow cobblestone streets of Sultanahmet. Visit the beautifully lit exterior of Hagia Sophia at dusk for atmospheric photos. Head to nearby Akbıyık Caddesi for a relaxed first dinner in Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite near the hotel upon arrival – try Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi for classic Turkish meatballs (köfte) with bread and ayran, a mid-range local staple (approx. ₺150–200 per person).
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant (inside Ottoman Imperial Hotel, Sultanahmet) – Ottoman-inspired cuisine with mezes and grilled meats in a historic setting. Mid-range pricing, approx. ₺400–600 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport (Turkcell or Vodafone kiosks in arrivals). Exchange some cash or use ATMs in Sultanahmet for Turkish Lira.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) when it opens – arrive early (8:30–9:00) to beat crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring this breathtaking 6th-century Byzantine basilica turned mosque. Marvel at the massive dome, golden mosaics, and layered history of Byzantine and Ottoman empires.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk directly across Sultanahmet Square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque). Explore its stunning interior with 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles and six minarets (note: closed during prayer times, check schedule). Afterward, visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) nearby – a hidden gem with stunning Byzantine floor mosaics.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Arasta Bazaar, a smaller, less touristy covered market behind the Blue Mosque selling quality ceramics, textiles, and spices. Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll along the Sea of Marmara waterfront (Kennedy Caddesi) to watch the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café Meşale in Sultanahmet – traditional Turkish breakfast spread with cheese, olives, eggs, simit, and çay (tea). Approx. ₺150–250.
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or Fuego Restaurant near the Hippodrome – pide (Turkish flatbread pizza), mercimek çorbası (lentil soup), and fresh salad. Approx. ₺200–300.
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant or Balıkçı Sabahattin (a beloved local fish restaurant in Sultanahmet) – fresh Bosphorus fish, mezes, and rakı. Approx. ₺500–700 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Mosque is free to enter but closed to tourists during the 5 daily prayer times (each closure lasts ~90 minutes). Check the day's prayer schedule in advance. Hagia Sophia entry is free for worshippers but tourists may need to pay a museum fee – verify current policy closer to travel date.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Topkapı Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) – the nerve center of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Explore the Imperial Council Chamber, the Harem (separate ticket), the Treasury (housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the stunning courtyards with Bosphorus views. Allow 3–4 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) complex, located just inside the Topkapı Palace grounds. Three museums in one: the main Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk. Highlights include the Alexander Sarcophagus and ancient Mesopotamian artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gülhane Park (adjacent to Topkapı) for a sunset stroll under rose gardens with Bosphorus views. Then explore the Cağaloğlu neighborhood for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Simit Sarayı bakery chain – simit (sesame-crusted bread ring), börek (flaky pastry), and tea. Quick and authentic. Approx. ₺80–150.
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapı Palace grounds – a historic canteen-style restaurant serving traditional Turkish dishes like lamb stew and pilaf. Convenient and atmospheric. Approx. ₺300–450.
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant in Eminönü (10-min taxi from Sultanahmet) – rooftop terrace with Golden Horn views, famous for southeastern Turkish kebabs (Urfa, Adana, lamb). Approx. ₺400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Topkapı Palace tickets online in advance to skip queues – the Harem requires a separate ticket and has limited daily entry. The Archaeological Museums are often overlooked but are world-class. Combined museum card (Müzekart) may offer savings if you plan many museum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) – one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Arrive when it opens at 8:30 to explore before crowds build. Browse carpets, ceramics, jewelry, spices, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills – it's expected and part of the culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes downhill to the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı / Egyptian Bazaar) in Eminönü. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and spices. Explore the lively Eminönü waterfront – watch fishermen on Galata Bridge and take in the chaotic, authentic energy of working Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry ride from Eminönü across the Golden Horn to Karaköy. Explore the hip neighborhood of Karaköy with its galleries, cafés, and street art. Walk up to the Galata Tower area for evening views.

meals.breakfast: Şükrü Usta (near Grand Bazaar) or Van Kahvaltı Evi (if you venture slightly further) – Van-style Kurdish breakfast with honey, clotted cream, and herb cheeses. Approx. ₺200–350.
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the famous floating boats at Eminönü waterfront – a true Istanbul street food experience. Add a glass of şalgam (fermented turnip juice) for the full effect. Approx. ₺80–120.
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası – a beloved neighborhood restaurant in Karaköy serving contemporary Turkish cuisine with excellent mezes and daily specials. Approx. ₺400–600.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Don't feel pressured to buy anything – browsing is perfectly acceptable. Keep your belongings secure in crowded market areas. The Eminönü-Karaköy ferry costs just a few lira and is a delightful micro-experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full Bosphorus Cruise. Board the public Şehir Hatları ferry from Eminönü (affordable, approx. ₺100–150 for the long round-trip) for the classic 6-hour cruise up the Bosphorus to Anadolu Kavağı village. Pass under the Bosphorus bridges, spot Rumeli and Anadolu fortresses, and watch the European and Asian shores unfold.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Anadolu Kavağı on the Asian shore. Hike up to the ruined Byzantine-Genoese Yoros Castle for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the charming fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to Eminönü (departs in late afternoon). Enjoy the golden-hour light on the water. Back in Sultanahmet, take a relaxing evening to rest or explore local tea houses.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – fuel up for a full day on the water.
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the seafood restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village – the village is famous for its fish restaurants. Order the catch of the day with salad and bread. Approx. ₺300–500.
meals.dinner: Cooking Alaturka (Sultanahmet) – a highly-regarded restaurant serving authentic home-style Anatolian dishes in a warm, intimate setting. Try the slow-cooked lamb and stuffed vegetables. Approx. ₺350–550.

day_by_day.notes: The public Şehir Hatları Bosphorus cruise departs Eminönü at set times (typically 10:35 and 13:35 in peak season). Check the current timetable at sehirhatlari.com.tr. Arrive 20 minutes early to secure a good outdoor deck seat. Bring sunscreen and a light layer for the breeze on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque – arguably the most architecturally magnificent mosque in Istanbul, designed by master architect Mimar Sinan in 1557. Explore the vast complex including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan. The surrounding neighborhood (Süleymaniye) offers stunning views over the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fatih district on foot – the old Byzantine neighborhood with traditional Istanbul life far from tourist crowds. Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) with its extraordinary 14th-century Byzantine mosaics and frescoes (check restoration status). Walk through the Fatih market streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via tram. Visit a traditional Turkish hammam (bath) for a cultural wellness experience. Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584, designed by Sinan) is a historic and mid-range option right in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Tarihi Kapalıçarşı Pidecisi or a local börekçi (pastry shop) near the hotel – börek, menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers), and tea. Approx. ₺150–200.
meals.lunch: Darüzziyafe Restaurant in the Süleymaniye complex – a beautifully restored Ottoman soup kitchen now serving traditional Ottoman cuisine. Atmospheric and mid-range. Approx. ₺350–500.
meals.dinner: Develi Restaurant (Samatya branch, 15-min taxi) – famous for southeastern Turkish cuisine, especially Gaziantep-style kebabs and baklava. Or dine lighter after the hammam at a local meyhane (tavern) near Sultanahmet. Approx. ₺400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Hammam etiquette: a basic bath + kese (exfoliation scrub) + massage package at Çemberlitaş runs approx. ₺600–900 for tourists. Book in advance online. Modest dress required for mosque visits – scarves provided at entrances. Chora Church restoration may still be ongoing; verify status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy (20-minute ferry, approx. ₺20). Explore Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) – a vibrant, authentic neighborhood market beloved by locals for fresh produce, cheese, olives, pickles, and street food. This is where real Istanbulites shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Moda neighborhood of Kadıköy – a charming, bohemian district with tree-lined streets, independent cafés, bookshops, and vintage stores. Walk along the Moda coastline with views back toward the European shore. Visit the Kadıköy Bull Statue (iconic local landmark) and browse the antique shops on Tellalzade Sokak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side via ferry at sunset – the crossing with the skyline of Sultanahmet glowing in the evening light is magical. Enjoy a relaxed evening dinner in Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab a simit from a street cart on the way to the ferry.
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy Market – one of Istanbul's most celebrated restaurants, serving rare Anatolian regional dishes that change daily. A culinary pilgrimage for food lovers. Approx. ₺300–450.
meals.dinner: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı (Beyoğlu, 20-min tram/taxi from Sultanahmet) – a classic ocakbaşı (open-fire grill) restaurant where you sit around the grill and watch your kebabs cook. Lively, authentic, excellent value. Approx. ₺400–600.

day_by_day.notes: Friday is Jumu'ah (Friday Prayer) – mosques will be very busy around midday (12:30–13:30). Plan mosque visits around this time. Kadıköy is a wonderful contrast to the tourist-heavy European side – embrace the local atmosphere and try as many market snacks as possible.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Beyoğlu and the Galata neighborhood. Start at Galata Tower (built 1348) – climb to the top for 360-degree panoramic views over Istanbul, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn. Then walk through the historic Jewish and Genoese quarter of Galata with its antique shops and art galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up the famous İstiklal Caddesi (Independence Avenue) – Istanbul's grand 1.4km pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European architecture, bookshops, cinemas, churches of multiple faiths, and the nostalgic red tram. Explore the atmospheric passages (Çiçek Pasajı, Avrupa Pasajı) branching off the main avenue. Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) for Ottoman-era paintings and rotating contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Beyoğlu for the evening – this is Istanbul's nightlife and dining heart. Explore the meyhane-lined Nevizade Sokak and Çiçek Pasajı for the classic Istanbul evening experience of mezes, rakı, and live music.

meals.breakfast: Mandabatmaz (near Galata, famous for its thick Turkish coffee) + a pastry from a nearby bakery. Approx. ₺100–150.
meals.lunch: Helvetia Lokanta on İstiklal – a beloved, no-frills lokanta (traditional canteen) serving daily home-cooked Turkish dishes. Order from the steam trays. Approx. ₺200–300.
meals.dinner: Nevizade Sokak meyhane crawl – pick one of the lively fish and meze taverns (Imroz, Boncuk, or Refik are classics) for a long, convivial dinner with fresh mezes, fish, and rakı. Approx. ₺500–800 with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Caddesi is extremely crowded on Saturday evenings – embrace the energy or visit slightly earlier in the afternoon. The Pera Museum charges a modest entry fee and is worth 1.5–2 hours. Nevizade Sokak meyhanes are best experienced slowly over 2–3 hours; they're as much about the atmosphere as the food.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) in Beşiktaş – the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace that replaced Topkapı as the imperial residence. Guided tours only; the palace contains 285 rooms, 46 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria). Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to the Beşiktaş waterfront along the Bosphorus. Explore the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel but the gardens are accessible) and the Yıldız Park – a vast forested park on the hillside above Beşiktaş with Ottoman pavilions, a lake, and wonderful city views. Visit the Yıldız Palace Museum within the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet via tram (Kabataş tram stop, then T1 tram line). Enjoy a quiet evening in the neighborhood – visit a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) in Gülhane Park for evening tea and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – Dolmabahçe tours start early, so fuel up properly.
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş market area (Sunday market is active) – grab a midye dolma (stuffed mussels sold by street vendors), a wrap, or eat at a local pide restaurant near the waterfront. Approx. ₺150–250.
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin (Sultanahmet) – if not visited earlier, this is one of Sultanahmet's finest traditional fish restaurants in a restored Ottoman house. Approx. ₺500–700. Or try Mozaik Restaurant for excellent Turkish cuisine in a cozy Sultanahmet setting.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires advance booking online – tours sell out, especially on weekends. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Yıldız Park is free to enter and is a wonderful escape from city noise. The Kabataş–Sultanahmet tram (T1 line) runs frequently and costs just a few lira.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) – a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, 1–1.5 hours by ferry from Eminönü. Visit Büyükada (the largest island) with its Victorian wooden mansions, horse-drawn carriages (phaeton), and pine forests. Rent a bicycle and explore the island at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take a phaeton up to the hilltop Monastery of Saint George (Aya Yorgi) for stunning views over the Marmara Sea and the Istanbul skyline in the distance. Explore the charming harbor town with its Greek Orthodox heritage, old mansions, and seaside cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Eminönü in the late afternoon/early evening. Enjoy the sea breeze and skyline views on the return journey. Quiet dinner back in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Grab a simit and tea at Eminönü before boarding the ferry – eat breakfast on the boat as Istanbul's skyline recedes behind you.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at one of the waterfront restaurants in Büyükada harbor – grilled fish, calamari, and salad with island views. Approx. ₺350–500.
meals.dinner: Giritli Restaurant (Sultanahmet) – a beloved restaurant specializing in Cretan-Greek-Turkish cuisine with unlimited mezes included. Intimate garden setting. Approx. ₺500–700.

day_by_day.notes: Şehir Hatları ferries run regularly from Eminönü and Kabataş to Büyükada. The journey takes about 90 minutes from Eminönü. Buy return tickets in advance. Bicycle rentals on the island are approx. ₺150–200/hour. The island is extremely popular on weekends – a Monday visit means significantly fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) – a magical 6th-century underground Byzantine cistern holding 80,000 cubic meters of water, supported by 336 columns. Recently renovated with artistic lighting installations. Located steps from Hagia Sophia. Allow 1–1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the lesser-visited but fascinating Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii) – a beautifully preserved 6th-century Byzantine church converted to a mosque, often called a miniature prototype of Hagia Sophia. Then visit the Sokollu Mehmet Pasha Mosque (another Sinan masterpiece) and wander through the quiet, authentic Kadırga neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take the T1 tram to Beyazıt and explore the Istanbul University area and the Second-Hand Book Bazaar (Sahaflar Çarşısı). End the evening at a rooftop bar or restaurant in Beyoğlu for panoramic night views.

meals.breakfast: Café İmren or a local pastane (pastry shop) near the hotel – fresh poğaça (soft savory buns), cheese pastries, and tea. Approx. ₺100–180.
meals.lunch: Havuzlu Restaurant inside the Grand Bazaar – a hidden gem with a courtyard fountain, serving Turkish home cooking. Approx. ₺250–400.
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant (Marmara Pera Hotel rooftop, Beyoğlu) – for a special mid-trip splurge, this acclaimed restaurant serves New Anatolian cuisine with breathtaking panoramic views. Approx. ₺800–1200. Alternatively, stay budget-conscious at a Beyoğlu meyhane for ₺400–600.

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern is best visited early morning to avoid tour groups. Little Hagia Sophia is free to enter and often completely uncrowded – a wonderful contrast to the main sites. If splurging on Mikla, book a table well in advance and request a window seat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods on the Golden Horn – two of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric districts with Greek Orthodox (Fener) and Jewish (Balat) heritage. Visit the stunning Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople (Greek Orthodox), the red-brick Phanar Greek Orthodox College, and the colorful painted houses of Balat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) if not visited earlier – or explore the Miniaturk open-air museum near the Golden Horn, which features 1:25 scale models of Turkey's greatest historical monuments (a fun and educational overview). Walk along the Golden Horn waterfront and cross the Atatürk Bridge for different perspectives.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet for a final full evening in the historic heart of the city. Visit the Sultanahmet area illuminated at night – the Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia, and Hippodrome are beautifully lit. Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of your favorite spots from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Forno Balat (a beloved bakery in Balat) – fresh bread, pastries, and excellent coffee in a hip neighborhood setting. A Balat institution. Approx. ₺150–250.
meals.lunch: Kuzguncuk Bostanı or a local Balat meyhane – explore the neighborhood lunch scene with fresh mezes, stuffed grape leaves, and seasonal vegetables. Approx. ₺250–400.
meals.dinner: Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Istanbul at Sultanahmet, a converted Ottoman prison) – for a memorable farewell dinner in extraordinary surroundings. Or revisit your favorite restaurant from the trip. Approx. ₺600–900.

day_by_day.notes: Fener and Balat are best explored on foot and are increasingly popular with photographers and food travelers. The neighborhoods are changing quickly, so some of the old-world charm exists alongside new cafés. Wear comfortable walking shoes – the streets are cobbled and hilly. The Golden Horn ferry (Haliç ferries) can be used to reach Fener from Eminönü cheaply.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul – revisit your favorite spot for one last look (Hagia Sophia at sunrise, Gülhane Park, or the Bosphorus waterfront). Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Arasta Bazaar (less hectic than Grand Bazaar) – quality ceramics, evil eye amulets (nazar boncuğu), Turkish delight, and saffron make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time – check out of the hotel and head to the airport. Allow 90 minutes for the journey from Sultanahmet to Istanbul Airport (IST) via Havaist bus or taxi, plus 2–3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. If flying from Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) on the Asian side, allow 60–90 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 remarkable days in one of the world's great cities.

meals.breakfast: A proper final Turkish breakfast at the hotel or at a neighborhood kahvaltı salonu – the full spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, tomatoes, cucumbers, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), simit, and endless çay. The perfect farewell to Istanbul.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout – a bowl of mercimek çorbası (red lentil soup) and fresh bread at a local lokanta. Approx. ₺150–200.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight.

day_by_day.notes: Leave extra time for checkout and luggage. Istanbul Airport (IST) is large – allow extra time post-security for walking to the gate. Consider purchasing a final box of Turkish delight from Hacı Bekir (the original Turkish delight maker since 1777, with a shop near the Grand Bazaar) as a farewell gift to yourself or others.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Sultanahmet district, Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Istanbul Airport to Historic Peninsula Boutique Stay in Sultanahmet via chauffeured Mercedes-Benz S-Class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into the boutique hotel (estimated arrival 14:30–15:00). Freshen up and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely orientation stroll around Sultanahmet Square — admire the exterior of the Blue Mosque, the Hippodrome of Constantinople, and the German Fountain. Absorb the atmosphere of the historic peninsula at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on the hotel rooftop or a nearby terrace bar with panoramic views of the Sea of Marmara and the Blue Mosque silhouette. Gentle first dinner in the neighbourhood to ease into Istanbul time.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant (inside Ottoman Imperial Kitchen, Sultanahmet) — refined Ottoman cuisine in a historic setting; tasting menu featuring dishes from 16th-century palace recipes, paired with Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag management is key. Confirm private transfer booking in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Carry cash in Turkish Lira for tips and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — skip-the-line VIP access with an expert archaeologist guide. Explore the Byzantine mosaics, imperial galleries, and the soaring dome in depth before the crowds build. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Topkapı Palace — private guided tour of the Imperial Harem, Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the sacred relics in the Pavilion of Holy Mantle. Stroll through the palace gardens overlooking the Bosphorus strait.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the Sirkeci district, followed by dinner at a premium restaurant with Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring börek, fresh cheeses, olives, sucuk, menemen, clotted cream with honey
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapı Palace grounds — a historic institution serving classic Turkish cuisine since 1897; try the lamb stew and baklava
meals.dinner: Tuğra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace Kempinski (short taxi ride) — iconic Ottoman-era palace dining on the Bosphorus; signature dishes include sea bass in vine leaves and Ottoman lamb rack

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapı Harem tickets in advance — they sell out quickly. Dress modestly for Hagia Sophia (shoulders and knees covered). Private guide recommended for maximum depth.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — explore the atmospheric underground Byzantine reservoir with its 336 marble columns and mysterious Medusa heads. Follow with a visit to the nearby Little Hagia Sophia (Küçük Ayasofya Camii), one of Istanbul's oldest and most beautiful mosques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive visit to the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex — three museums in one: the Archaeological Museum, the Museum of the Ancient Orient, and the Tiled Kiosk Museum. Private curator-led tour of highlights including the Alexander Sarcophagus and Treaty of Kadesh.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the atmospheric backstreets of Sultanahmet at dusk. Pre-dinner aperitif at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Seasons Restaurant at Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet — elegant Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine in a converted 19th-century prison; set lunch menu with local seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant (Edirnekapı, short taxi) — the world's only restaurant dedicated to recreating Ottoman palace banquet recipes from 15th–17th century; extraordinary tasting menu experience

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeological Museums are often overlooked by tourists — a true hidden gem. Book Asitane well in advance. Comfortable walking shoes essential for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Private Bosphorus breakfast cruise — depart from Eminönü or Kabataş pier on a chartered private yacht. Sail past Dolmabahçe Palace, Beylerbeyi Palace, Ottoman waterfront mansions (yalıs), and the Rumeli and Anadolu fortresses. Breakfast served on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Bebek or Arnavutköy on the European shore. Explore the charming neighbourhood on foot — boutique shops, art galleries, and waterfront cafés. Visit the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) — a dramatic 15th-century Ottoman fortification built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Sultanahmet by private car. Hammam experience at Çemberlitaş Hamamı — one of Istanbul's most historic bathhouses, designed by Sinan in 1584; book the private VIP suite with personal attendant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast served on the private yacht — fresh pastries, fruit, cheeses, eggs, Turkish tea and coffee
meals.lunch: Poseidon Restaurant in Bebek — legendary seafood restaurant on the Bosphorus waterfront; grilled sea bass, stuffed mussels, and meze platters
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant (Beyoğlu, short taxi) — Michelin-recommended, rooftop fine dining with panoramic Istanbul views; Chef Mehmet Gürs' modern Anatolian cuisine with Nordic influences

day_by_day.notes: Charter the private yacht through your hotel concierge or a specialist operator (minimum 3 hours recommended). Book Çemberlitaş VIP suite in advance. Bring a light jacket for the evening Bosphorus breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Expert guide navigates you to the finest artisan workshops for hand-painted ceramics, antique jewellery, silk textiles, and hand-woven carpets. Avoid tourist traps with insider knowledge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) — explore stalls piled high with saffron, sumac, dried fruits, Turkish delight, and rare spices. Purchase premium spices and lokum (Turkish delight) as gifts. Stroll along the Golden Horn waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Pierre Loti Hill viewpoint — take the historic cable car up for sweeping views over the Golden Horn. Named after the French novelist who frequented the hilltop café.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar — a legendary Istanbul institution since 1901, serving classic Turkish dishes in a beautiful tiled dining room; lamb chops, börek, and rice pudding
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant (Tomtom Suites, Beyoğlu) — intimate fine dining with a creative Turkish-Mediterranean tasting menu; exceptional wine list featuring Anatolian varietals

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected in the Grand Bazaar — your guide will assist. The bazaar is closed on Sundays. Wear comfortable shoes. Bring a reusable bag for purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — private ferry from Kabataş pier to Büyükada, the largest island. No motorised vehicles allowed; hire a private horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) for a tour of the Victorian-era wooden mansions and the Monastery of St. George on the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim or relax at a private beach club on Büyükada. Explore the island's charming town centre — rent bicycles for a leisurely coastal ride. Enjoy the peaceful contrast to bustling Istanbul.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul at sunset. Rest and refresh at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early, to catch the morning ferry)
meals.lunch: Milto Restaurant on Büyükada — the island's finest seafood restaurant; grilled octopus, sea bream, and fresh meze with Aegean white wine on the waterfront terrace
meals.dinner: In-hotel dining or room service — a relaxed evening after the day trip; request the hotel's chef's tasting menu if available

day_by_day.notes: Ferries run regularly from Kabataş; private charter available for maximum flexibility. The island is popular on weekends — weekday visits are more serene. Sunscreen and a hat are essential. The hike to St. George Monastery takes about 45 minutes each way.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — the masterpiece of Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, built for Suleiman the Magnificent. Explore the mosque interior, the tombs of Suleiman and Roxelana, the historic medrese (theological school), and the panoramic terrace overlooking the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Zeyrek and Fatih neighbourhoods on foot with a private guide — discover Byzantine-era churches converted to mosques, Ottoman wooden houses, and authentic working-class Istanbul life far from tourist routes. Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) with its breathtaking Byzantine mosaics and frescoes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Whirling Dervishes ceremony (Sema) at the Hodjapasha Cultural Centre or Galata Mevlevi Lodge — a deeply spiritual and mesmerising Sufi ritual. Book premium reserved seating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Develi Restaurant (Samatya) — a celebrated Istanbul institution since 1912 specialising in southeastern Turkish cuisine; Gaziantep-style kebabs, lahmacun, and katmer dessert
meals.dinner: Çiya Sofrası (Kadıköy, Asian side — short ferry ride) — legendary restaurant by Chef Musa Dağdeviren, dedicated to preserving rare Anatolian recipes; extraordinary depth of Turkish culinary heritage

day_by_day.notes: Dress code for the mosque: shoulders and knees covered, shoes removed. The Whirling Dervishes ceremony is deeply respectful — maintain silence and avoid flash photography. Book ceremony tickets well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided exploration of Beyoğlu district — cross the Galata Bridge on foot, visit the historic Galata Tower (14th century Genoese tower with panoramic city views). Explore the atmospheric Galata neighbourhood with its antique shops, vintage record stores, and independent bookshops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up İstiklal Avenue — the grand pedestrian boulevard of modern Istanbul. Visit the historic Pera Museum with its collection of Orientalist paintings including Osman Hamdi Bey's 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Explore the elegant 19th-century Pera Palace Hotel — have afternoon tea in the Orient Bar, where Agatha Christie wrote 'Murder on the Orient Express.'
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails in Beyoğlu's vibrant bar scene, followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Karaköy Lokantası — a beloved neighbourhood restaurant in Karaköy serving elevated traditional Turkish home cooking; daily-changing menu of mezes and slow-cooked mains
meals.dinner: Neolokal Restaurant (SALT Galata building) — Chef Maksut Aşkar's pioneering modern Anatolian cuisine; innovative tasting menu drawing on forgotten Ottoman and Anatolian ingredients; James Beard-nominated

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is extremely busy on weekends — morning visits are more pleasant. The Pera Palace Hotel afternoon tea must be booked in advance. Galata Tower has a queue — pre-purchase tickets online.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace on the Bosphorus, blending European Baroque with Ottoman aesthetics. Highlights include the 4.5-ton Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria), the Ceremonial Hall, and the Harem quarters. Atatürk died here in 1938 — his room is preserved.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern Museum (İstanbul Modern) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum, recently relocated to a stunning new Renzo Piano-designed building on the Bosphorus waterfront at Karaköy. Private curator-led tour of the permanent collection and special exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Bosphorus cruise on a private gulet (traditional wooden yacht) — champagne and canapés served on deck as you sail past illuminated palaces and bridges.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Laledan Restaurant at Çırağan Palace Kempinski — elegant terrace dining directly on the Bosphorus; refined Turkish and Mediterranean cuisine with exceptional views of the water
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner cruise on the private gulet — premium catering with meze platters, grilled seafood, Turkish wines, and baklava for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık (public rooms) and Harem — book both. Photography restrictions inside. The Istanbul Modern is closed on Mondays. Private gulet charter: 2–3 hours recommended for sunset timing.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private Turkish cooking class — held in a traditional Ottoman-style kitchen in Sultanahmet or Beyoğlu. Learn to prepare a full Turkish feast: mezes (hummus, haydari, patlıcan salatası), main courses (lamb güveç, stuffed peppers), and desserts (baklava, sütlaç). Taught by a professional chef with market sourcing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mosaic Museum (Büyük Saray Mozaikleri Müzesi) — located steps from the hotel in Sultanahmet, housing extraordinary 5th–6th century Byzantine floor mosaics from the Great Palace of Constantinople. Then explore the Arasta Bazaar — a quieter, more authentic alternative to the Grand Bazaar, specialising in quality ceramics and textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private calligraphy or Turkish miniature painting workshop with a master artist — a unique cultural experience creating your own artwork to take home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during the morning cooking class — the class culminates in a shared meal with Turkish wines or ayran
meals.dinner: Balıkçı Sabahattin (Sultanahmet) — Istanbul's most celebrated traditional fish restaurant, family-run since 1927; whole grilled fish, exceptional meze, and rakı in a charming historic building

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one week in advance through your hotel concierge. The calligraphy workshop can be arranged through the Caligra Istanbul studio. Balıkçı Sabahattin is cash-only — bring Turkish Lira.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Edirne (2.5 hours by private car) — the former Ottoman capital. Visit the Selimiye Mosque, considered Mimar Sinan's greatest masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site — even more architecturally refined than the Blue Mosque. Tour with a specialist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Edirne's historic centre — the Old Mosque (Eski Cami), the Bedesten covered market, and the Macedonian Tower. Edirne is famous for its unique liver kebab (ciğer) and oil wrestling tradition. Visit the Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car (arrive approximately 19:00–19:30). Relaxed evening in Sultanahmet.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast (early departure recommended by 07:30)
meals.lunch: Melek Anne Restaurant in Edirne — the city's most acclaimed restaurant; try the legendary Edirne-style fried liver (tava ciğeri), white cheese, and local specialities
meals.dinner: Hamdi Restaurant (Eminönü, Istanbul) — panoramic rooftop views of the Golden Horn and Bosphorus; southeastern Turkish cuisine with exceptional kebabs and mezes; a classic Istanbul institution

day_by_day.notes: Private car with driver is the most comfortable option for Edirne. Depart early to maximise time there. Edirne is an underrated gem — most tourists never visit. Selimiye Mosque dress code applies.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Topkapı Palace Treasury and Imperial Armoury for a more in-depth second visit with a different expert guide focusing on the collection's historical context. Then explore the Gülhane Park — the former outer garden of Topkapı Palace, one of Istanbul's oldest and most beautiful public parks in spring bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Kadıköy neighbourhood on the Asian side of Istanbul — a 20-minute ferry ride from Eminönü. Wander the vibrant Kadıköy market (Tarihi Kadıköy Pazarı) — an extraordinary sensory experience with fresh produce, spices, cheeses, and street food. Visit the Moda neighbourhood for its charming waterfront promenade and café culture.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury farewell hammam experience at the Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — the most historic and beautifully restored hammam in Istanbul, built by Sinan in 1556 for Roxelana. Book the premium private suite for an extended 2-hour ritual.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Çiya Kebap (Kadıköy) — sister restaurant to Çiya Sofrası; extraordinary regional kebabs and stews from across Anatolia; a pilgrimage for serious food lovers
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner at 360 Istanbul (İstiklal Avenue rooftop) — iconic panoramic rooftop restaurant with 360-degree views of Istanbul; creative Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine; exceptional cocktail bar

day_by_day.notes: The Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı is the most prestigious hammam in Istanbul — book the private suite at least 2 weeks in advance. The Kadıköy market is at its best on weekday mornings. Return from Asian side by ferry — the crossing at sunset is magical.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — slow, luxurious start. Enjoy an extended hotel breakfast. Last visit to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) for a peaceful early-morning prayer-time visit when it is quietest and most atmospheric. Sit quietly in the courtyard and absorb the beauty of the 17th-century masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir and gift shopping — return to the Arasta Bazaar or Grand Bazaar for any last purchases: premium Turkish carpets, hand-painted Iznik ceramics, saffron, premium lokum, or antique jewellery. Hotel check-out and private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — flight home. In-airport dining at the premium lounges of Istanbul Airport (ISL), which are among the finest in the world.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — savour every last detail: fresh simit, clotted cream, honey, börek, and çay
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Sultanahmet) — an elegant final meal in the heart of the historic peninsula; seasonal tasting menu with Turkish wine pairings
meals.dinner: Istanbul Airport Turkish Airlines CIP Lounge or IGA Airport Lounge — world-class lounge dining with hot and cold Turkish specialities, open bar, and premium service

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in (Istanbul Airport is large and requires significant transit time). Confirm private transfer booking the night before. Excess baggage allowance may be needed for purchases — check airline policy. Keep valuables and purchased items in carry-on luggage.
